en:
...It's kind of lonely, huh.
It's finally down to just three of us.
The people telling stories keep disappearing one after another...
So I'm up next, huh.
I know I shouldn't say it myself, but I think I'm a pretty cheerful girl.
...But right now I'm in kind of a gloomy mood.
I wonder if something will happen to me too once I tell my story.{p}

...Well, there's no point thinking about stuff like that.
Let's cheer up and get going!
{c}{f:|}, can you swim?
I can swim
I can't swim
I'm great at the dog paddle, at least
Oh, so you can swim.{p}

Right?
It'd be embarrassing to be in high school and still not know how to swim.
{f:As for me|Me}, {f:if I ever get a boyfriend,|I'd really like my boyfriend} {f:I want one who can swim|to be able to swim too}.
Why, you ask?
Isn't it obvious?
Otherwise it'd be no fun going to the beach together.
And if I started drowning, who would save me?
Plus, I totally want to travel abroad.
I want to spend time alone with my boyfriend at some resort on a tropical island.
So he has to be able to swim, or no deal.{p}

...Oh, sorry.
I got off topic.
We were talking about the swim club.
Actually, my big sister went to this school before me.

She's seven years older than me.
And she was in the girls' swim club.
The boys' and girls' clubs are separate, see.
That's how I know this story.
Back when my sister was there, there was this incredible swimmer, apparently.
Everyone said she swam like a fish, or so I heard.
That's how good a swimmer she was.
They say when she swam, the water rippled like it was happy.
Everyone was spellbound, apparently.
It's not like the water was really happy, of course.
It's just that her swimming was so graceful, it wouldn't be strange if it looked that way.{p}

Her name was Yuko Seto.
If you'd said Seto was a fish reborn, everyone would've believed it.
But even someone like Seto died in an accident.
One day, she had a heart attack while she was swimming.{p}

By the time everyone rushed over in shock to save her, it was already too late.
Scary, right?{p}

They say even monkeys fall out of trees, but nobody ever dreamed Seto of all people would drown.
So nobody could believe she was really dead.
And it was after that.
That strange things started happening.{p}Hey, hey, what kind of strange things do you think happened?
Someone is heard swimming in the empty pool
The empty club room ends up soaking wet
More people get leg cramps while swimming

That's right.
Apparently there started to be signs that someone had used the club room when nobody should have been there.
You tidy up the club room nice and neat, right?
Then the next day, the club room is flooded with water.
There are water droplets on the walls and everything, like someone splashed water all over.
Naturally, everyone started talking.
They said it had to be Seto's ghost.
That Seto couldn't forget the swim club, and was coming back to haunt it.
And on top of that, the girls who used her locker had accidents, one after another.{p}

They'd suddenly get leg cramps or start drowning while swimming.
It only happened to girls who'd used Seto's locker.
And when you asked them about it, they'd all say the same thing.
That while they were swimming, someone suddenly grabbed their legs and pulled.{p}

...It's gotta be Seto.
Seto's lonely, and she wants friends.
So I think she pulls the legs of the girls who use her locker.
Because she thinks they can become friends.
The girls who got pulled would be creeped out and switch lockers right away, right?
At first, though, a lot of girls wanted to use that locker just for fun, apparently.{p}

I mean, it had belonged to Seto, the ace of the girls' swim club.
A weird rumor went around that whoever used it would get better at swimming.
But way too many weird things kept happening, right?
So in the end, nobody used it anymore.
It's not like anyone got better at swimming anyway.
Well, obviously.{p}

So, that locker got banned.
Moving it is creepy, and nobody wants to touch it, right?
Then the rumor grew and grew, and now they say just opening Seto's locker will bring you bad luck.
It's the never-opened locker, you could say.
Scary, huh?
I don't get how anyone who knows that story would want to join the swim club.
But you're a little curious about that locker, right?{p}No?
I'm curious
I'm not really curious

Right?
To tell you the truth, I'm curious too.
But everybody says they're not interested.
...I've been looking for someone who was.
I mean, don't you want to find out whether there really is a cursed locker?{p}
Hey, let's go check it out together, right now!
Go check it out
No way, I don't want to

That's it, {f:guys|girls} gotta have guts, right?
We've just gotta go!{p}

...Whoa, it's soaking wet.
Don't they clean up properly?
Or maybe this is Seto's curse.
Wow, there are a lot of lockers.
I heard Seto's locker was somewhere on the right side... but I don't know exactly which one.{p}

Looks like there are eight lockers on the right side.
We don't know which one, so let's just open them one by one.
...I wonder what'll happen when we open it.
Maybe Seto's ghost will come out.
...Apparently the girls' swim club these days is told never to open it.
Someone must have opened it and something horrible happened.
But you'll be fine, right, {c}{f:|}?
Are you ready?{p}So, which one should we open?
The one on the far right
Second from the right
Third from the right
Fourth from the right
Fifth from the right
Sixth from the right
Seventh from the right
The one on the far left
"{f:Waaagh|Eeek}!"{p}
{f:I|I} screamed before I knew it.{p}
"Eeeeek!"{p}

Fukuzawa slammed the locker door shut.
Then, staring hard at {f:me|me}, she murmured in a trembling voice.{p}

"...Did you see that?
You saw that, right?"
She was looking to {f:me|me} for agreement.
{f:I|I} nodded.
Then I turned my eyes to the locker once more.{p}

"...H-hey.
Want to open it again?"
Suddenly, Fukuzawa asked me something terrifying.
We'd just seen what was in there, and she wanted to see it again...
But if we opened it again, what {f:would|would} happen?{p}What should I do?
Don't open it again
Try opening it once more

"Let's just go back, Fukuzawa."
{f:I|I} tugged her by the hand.{p}

"...Aw, too bad.
And here I thought you had more guts, {c}{f:|}.
{f:At this rate|If you'd snapped a picture or something}, {f:you'll never get a girlfriend|it would've made a great scoop}."
{f:I|I} {f:laughed|smiled wryly} at her words as I left the swim club room.{p}

I {f:have|have} to hurry back to the newspaper club.
And hear the next story.
If the seventh person doesn't show up, the next story will be the last.
I'll {f:get|get} this gathering over with as fast as I can.
...And then I'll {f:forget|forget} what I just saw.{p}

I leaped back without thinking.
What is this thing?!{p}
"Eeeeeeeeeek!"{p}

"Fukuzawa!"
Fukuzawa couldn't get away from that thing.
I heard her scream, and before I could even blink, she was dragged into the locker.
By the time I shouted, she was already inside.
"Fukuzawa!"{p}

When I shouted again and reached out to save her, the locker slammed shut with a sound like a scream.
What should I do?
Open it?{p}Or else...
Open it
Call Fukuzawa's name
Leave it alone
"Are you okay?!"{p}

I yanked on the locker with all my strength.
...But it wouldn't budge.
It was a narrow locker, barely big enough for one person.
What on earth was going on in there...{p}
At the same time, I heard a horrible sound, dull and muffled, a grinding crunch like bones being crushed.{p}

Something was breaking in there.
I could hear it snapping and cracking, like something being folded up.{p}
The locker shook violently, back and forth, side to side.{p}
"Gueh... ehhh......"{p}

My heart clenched as I heard an agonized groan, as if wrung out of someone's throat.
It had changed so horribly that it no longer sounded like Fukuzawa's voice at all.
But there was no mistaking it.
It had to be Fukuzawa's voice.{p}
"Fukuzawa!
Fukuzawa!"{p}

I pounded on the locker with all my strength, hard enough to break it.
...But there was no longer any answer.{p}

Instead of words, only an eerie sound came from inside the locker.
Was that the sound of something eating...?{p}
Or the sound of something being crushed...?{p}
Suddenly, there was a loud clunk.{p}

Then the locker door swung open, just a little.
At the same moment, that sickening sound stopped.
...What should I do?
Should I open it and look inside?{p}Did I have the courage to see what was in there?
Open it
Don't open it

I swallowed hard and put my hand on the locker.
Then I slowly pulled the door open.{p}

It made the dull grinding sound of rusted metal.
Had locker doors always been this heavy...?{p}

The locker door came open.
...Inside......there was nothing.
The inside of the locker had been neatly cleaned out. It was empty.
...A strong smell of iron drifted out of it.
The smell of iron.
You could also call it the smell of blood.
But the inside of the locker was only a little chipped at the corners. There wasn't a single trace of blood.
...Maybe it really was just the smell of iron.{p}
Someone tapped me on the shoulder from behind, and I jumped, trembling.{p}

I turned around, and there stood the last one.
"So it's finally come down to just the two of us."
The last one seemed to be smiling, somehow.
I nodded in silence.
He looked like he wanted to say something, but his mouth kept working, as if the words were hard to get out.{p}

He seemed to make up his mind; he looked down, then peered up at me and asked,
"...What will you do?
Are you still going to keep going?"
What should I do?
The people who told their stories were vanishing, one after another.
Could this still be called a coincidence?
If I kept on like this, even he, the last one left, would probably vanish too.
And then what would become of me, the last one left behind...?
Was it really all right to keep going?{p}Or should I stop while I still had my life?
Keep going
Stop

"Let's keep going."
I said it firmly.
He stayed silent.
Then he slowly let out a long breath.{p}

"...I see.
You're quite something.
From the first time I saw you, I thought you were no ordinary person.
It seems you have something in you... something ordinary people shouldn't have."
I didn't understand what he meant.
He kept on smiling, just as before.
"...Well then, shall we go back to the newspaper club?"
There was no point in staying here.
Reiko Fukuzawa had vanished.
She wasn't here anymore.
I didn't even have a way of finding out whether she was dead or alive.{p}

"Let's not go back to the newspaper club."
The last one left suddenly spoke up.
"Why don't we go to the old school building now?"
That was what he added.
Why did we have to go to the old school building?
"The old school building?"
I tilted my head.
"That's right, the old school building.
I'm the only one left who has to tell a story, right?
Then we have to go to the old school building.
The story I'm going to tell is about the old school building.
...You see, I wasn't sure whether I should tell this story, but I think now is the time I should.
That's why we absolutely have to go to the old school building."
He smiled meaningfully.
A story that meant we had to go to the old school building?
What on earth could it be?{p}

Outside, it was already dark.
What time was it, anyway?
I couldn't see a clock anywhere around.
Neither he nor I had a wristwatch.{p}...What should I do?
Go to the old school building
Go back to the newspaper club

"...All right.
Let's go."
When he heard my answer, he seemed relieved, and his face broke into a broad smile.
"I thought you'd say that.
I was sure that you, of all people, would say that."{p}

With that, he set off briskly ahead of me.
I followed behind him in silence.{p}

...I thought I heard laughter behind me.
What was waiting for me in the old school building?{p}

Hmm...
So you can't swim?
Then I guess you hate pools, huh.
Me, I love them.
My big sister loves them too.
Actually, my big sister went to this school before us, see.{p}

Whoa, {c}{f:|}, so you're good at the dog paddle?
Doesn't dog paddling make your neck tired?
It's not like I can't do it, but doing it for a long time is tough.
And you're actually good at it? I'm impressed.
Next time, I'm gonna have you coach me.{p}That's okay, right?
I'd be glad to
Let me think about it a little

You want to think about it?
Ahahaha.
{c}{f:|}, are you getting flustered?
I know, what you said a minute ago was a joke, right?
It wasn't very funny.
I was asking you seriously and you answered with a lame joke, so I was just paying you back. I may not look it, but I'm actually a good swimmer.
I even went to swimming school.
But the way I swim isn't the competition kind, all about times and form.
I learned emergency swimming, like putting clothes on and taking them off underwater, or swimming with your shoes still on.
It's about how to save yourself with whatever's around you, like when a ship sinks or you fall into the sea.
You're laughing, {c}{f:|}, but swimming in your clothes takes a lot of stamina.
One T-shirt is no trouble at all, but emergencies happen in sweatshirt and sweater season too, you know.
If you don't practice properly, you'll drown under the weight of your own clothes.
...Hee hee, looks like you get it now.{p}

Okay then, back to the story.
It was about the swim club, right?{p}

Really?
Yay, I'm so happy.
In class they teach you the crawl and the breaststroke, but they never teach you the dog paddle, huh.
And you know what? At this school, the dog paddle is taboo.{p}

Why? Because something horrible happened here before...
What I'm going to tell you about is an incident that happened at this school just a few years ago.
It's a story about the swim club.
You see, I have a sister who's seven years older than me, and she was a student here too.
She was in the girls' swim club.
So this is a story I heard from my sister.{p}

Seto sneered at those boys,
"Oh my, what's this?
You call that swimming?
I bet even a dog would be faster."
That's how she taunted them, apparently.
Ugh, elites.
Anyone below their level, they don't even count as human.
Well, even so, the boys were used to Seto's nasty remarks, so it would just end with,
"Oh brother, here we go again."
and that was that.{p}

But you see, right at that time a stray dog had gotten onto the school grounds and was wandering around near the pool.
It was one of the boys who spotted the stray, they say.{p}

The stray took one look at the pool, brimming with water, and dove straight in.
It really was a hot day.
A dog is basically wearing a fur coat, right?
That dog had been staggering from heatstroke, but as soon as it hit the water it perked right up and started swimming, they say.
The boys had all climbed out onto the poolside and were watching, amused, but the girls, who were wrapped up in practice, panicked when a stray dog suddenly came in.{p}
Just when they were starting to think it was about time to chase the dog out,

"Kyaaaaaaaah☆"
an especially loud scream went up.{p}

It was Seto's voice.
Everyone looked toward it at once.{p}

In the middle of the pool, Seto and the stray were thrashing around, splashing up water.
At first glance it looked like she was playing with the dog, but the water around them was ringed with red...{p}

Seto went limp and stopped moving.
Dogs have an instinct to chase anything that runs away.
The faster it runs, the harder they go after it.
That's why it went after Seto.
After that, the pool was in even more of a panic, they say.
The teachers came running, and only then did they finally manage to catch the stray.
Seto was already dead.
She bled to death from the bite wounds, they say.
Several other people got hurt too, and the swim club couldn't practice for a while.
The boys' side is still disbanded, even now.
And they say every boy who was a member back then got expelled.{p}

As for the girls' side, it started up again as a club when my sister was a third-year, I hear, but they had a hard time getting members.
It was so plain and dull, you'd never believe it was the same glorious girls' swim club as before.
It was all people who'd swim a bit and then start goofing around in the water, and everyone who wanted to swim seriously transferred to other schools.
My sister wasn't that into swimming, so she stayed in the swim club here.
And you know, the one who made the dog paddle taboo was my sister.{p}

That day was a hot one too, apparently.
Everyone was playing around instead of practicing.
Then one of the girls showed off a dog paddle as a joke.
"Back in this pool, a while ago..."
she said, gossiping about that incident.{p}

And then that girl got a cramp in her leg.
Everyone laughed and said that's what she got for spreading tasteless gossip, but when they saw her ankle, they all went quiet.{p}

On her ankle, there was a clear set of dog tooth marks.
Blood was faintly oozing out, just as if she'd really been bitten...
Everyone agreed.
This had to be Seto's curse.
Seto was angry, they said, because she didn't want people gossiping about her for fun.
So my sister made the dog paddle taboo in this pool.
Not so much to keep people from getting hurt, but to let Seto rest in peace.{p}

A hand, just a hand, is sticking up out of the pool, they say.
It was a teacher who found it first, apparently, while doing the after-school rounds...
The teacher thought someone was drowning and reached out to help.
And then...{p}

The hand in the pool slipped right back down into the water.
It wasn't the hand of someone drowning, they say.
When the girls in the swim club heard about it, they figured it out right away.
That was the hand of Seto's ghost.
It was Seto, holding out her hand for help.
And so a rumor spread that the way to lay her soul to rest was to grab the ghost's hand when it came out of the pool and pull her up.{p}

After that, younger students and boys who'd admired Seto kept going to the pool and trying to grab the hand.
But it was no use.
Whenever someone tried to grab it, the hand would pull back right away.
The girls in the swim club tried everything they could to save her soul.
And so they came to this conclusion.
Maybe she wanted to be saved by one particular person.
She pulled her hand back, they thought, as a way of saying she wanted someone else to help her.{p}

Then you'd wonder whose help she wanted, right?
So first, they decided that everyone in the girls' swim club would reach out one by one and try to take her hand.
Of course, some of them were scared.
But the captain of the girls' swim club talked everyone into it.{p}

All the members snuck into the pool at night.
Damp air, and a steamy heat...
It was the kind of night that makes your whole body feel heavy, they say.
The pool lay full of still water.
"Will her hand really come out...?"
Some of the members had never actually seen the hand, so a few of them were restless and fidgety.
And then...
They heard the sound of water.{p}

"Ah!"
one of the members cried out.
That hand had come up out of the pool.
"Seto☆"
Everyone rushed over to the hand.
And one by one, with all their hearts, they reached out over the pool.
But the hand sticking out of the water still refused every hand they offered.
And once several of them had tried...{p}

"Kyaaaaah☆"
one girl screamed.
She was the swim club's great hope.
She was the best swimmer after Seto, see.
Her name was Hayashi.{p}

When she held out her hand, the hand from the pool didn't pull back.
But...{p}

"Nooooo☆"
She cried out loud and clutched her head.
Everyone was startled and ran over to her.
Had Seto's hand chosen her, and had something terrible happened?
That's what they thought.
And then...{p}

But it vanished right away, they say.
...Do you know what a living spirit is?{p}

It's when a living person's grudges or jealousy take on a ghostlike form and appear.
I think that's what showed up in the pool.
Wasn't it Hayashi's living spirit in the water?
Maybe Hayashi's living spirit was trying to drown anyone who swam better than her.
They say Seto died of a heart attack, but...
Maybe it was Hayashi's living spirit that caused it... just kidding.
I shouldn't say things like that?
But I can't help thinking it.{p}

That the hands coming out of the pool weren't asking for help at all...
That maybe they were looking for the next person to drag under... that's what I think.
They say Hayashi set one school record after another before she graduated.
There were other girls who looked like they might set records too, but...
Apparently they all said the same thing.
When it really counted, something pulled at their legs and they couldn't swim right... they said.{p}

Gives you chills, doesn't it?
Sure, just seeing Hayashi's figure wavering in the pool water with a hand reaching out of it isn't hard proof.
Maybe her reflection just happened to be on the water, and some ghost's hand or something came out of it, that's all.
But...
I'm going with the theory that it was Hayashi's living spirit.
Hey, {c}{f:|}, what do you think?{p}What do you think that figure of Hayashi wavering in the pool at night really was?
Hayashi was just reflected in the water
It must have been Hayashi's living spirit

Huh?
Why would you say that?{p}

Right.
That's the only explanation, isn't it?
But if it wasn't...
Then maybe Hayashi had it a bit rough.
I mean...
The living-spirit theory about her got pretty famous.
And it seems she got harassed a lot because of it.
The girls who said something grabbed their legs in the pool and kept them from setting records were bullying her too.
It was pretty brutal, apparently.
Fights between girls can get scary{f:, you know.|, right?}
If the hand coming out of the pool was actually Seto's ghost...
Then Hayashi was framed for something she didn't do.
Having died herself, Seto envied Hayashi for becoming the swim club's top swimmer, and tormented her.
Then she got in the way of anyone who might set a record, too, and pinned it all on Hayashi...
Just kidding.
That's not it, right?
It's Hayashi's living spirit that's to blame, isn't it?
After all, you said so too, {c}{f:|}.
I bet everyone else thinks so too.
Well then, shall we move on to the next story?
Come on, whose turn is it next...?{p}

That's right.
More and more people started getting cramps in their legs while swimming.
And it was always someone swimming in Lane 4.
Lane 4 was the lane Seto used to swim in.
Our school's pool has eight lanes, right?
Apparently at swim meets, swimmers are placed from the center lanes outward, fastest times first.
Seto practiced in Lane 4 all the time, not just at meets.
And Lane 4 was where Seto died, too.
These days they call Lane 4 the Lane of Death and nobody will swim in it, but back then, the swim club members all dreamed of swimming in that lane.
They wanted to swim as fast and gracefully as Seto, so they practiced in Lane 4 like they were fighting over it.{p}

Everyone could put up with a little leg cramp.
But after a while, it stopped being just leg cramps.{p}

The girl swimming in Lane 4 that day was named Hayashi; she'd been Seto's rival.
With Seto gone, she'd become the swim club's great hope, but her times just weren't improving.
So maybe she was hoping some of Seto's luck would rub off on her?
She went to the pool earlier than the other members and claimed Lane 4 for herself.{p}

Hayashi swam alone, silently.
But after a while, she noticed something strange.{p}What was it...?
Something pulled at her legs
She felt someone watching her
Someone was following behind her

Someone was following behind her, you see.
While she swam, she could see a figure at the edge of her vision.
She thought it was another member, but the figure seemed to be swimming in Lane 4.
I was here first!
Thinking that, she stopped to tell off whoever was coming up behind her.{p}
And then...★{p}

"Huh, I must've imagined it."
This is where someone died, after all.
I'm just a little on edge, that's all.
She told herself that and started swimming again.{p}

But as she swam, there it was again: someone's figure flickering in and out at the edge of her eye.
It's my imagination, just my imagination.
Hayashi kept swimming, muttering that to herself.
But soon she couldn't tell herself that anymore.
The figure was gradually getting closer.
The shadow she'd only glimpsed at the edge of her vision was now just one body length behind her!
And I haven't slowed my pace at all...
At this rate, it's going to catch me!{p}What should she do?★
Escape into the next lane
Pick up her pace and pull away

She must have been scared of whatever was coming up behind her, but she also had her pride as the swim club's great hope.
She picked up her pace, trying to pull away from the shadow in one burst.
And it seemed to work.
The shadow fell further and further behind.
But Hayashi didn't slow down one bit.
She was still uneasy, after all.
But no matter how long she fled, the unease wouldn't go away.
How far do I have to swim...?
The wall should be coming up soon...
The moment she thought that☆{p}

She saw that figure from before, right by her shoulder.
It was Seto.
Seto's graceful form, exactly the same as when she was alive.
Am I going to lose to Seto again?
Anything but that!
The instant she thought that...{p}

"Ow!☆"
Hayashi slammed full force into the pool wall.
She'd smashed her right arm, the one stroking through the water, straight into it.
As Hayashi's mind went blank with pain, Seto's voice rang in her ears.
"Oh, too bad.
The fish got away..."
That's what it said.{p}

Hayashi's arm only had a cracked bone, and they said once it healed it wouldn't affect her swimming at all, but she was completely terrified.
In the end, she quit swimming.
They say she's married now, an ordinary housewife.
After Hayashi, three people went missing at that pool.
Every one of them had been practicing in Lane 4.
When you think about that, maybe Hayashi made the right choice.
It's a shame about all that talent, though.{p}

I wonder what happened to the ones who went missing?
All there is to go on is
"The fish got away..."
those words of Seto's.
Maybe Seto ate them, or maybe they're being kept in a fish tank...
Either way, I don't think they're in this world anymore.{p}

Hee hee hee.
Your class has swimming in P.E. tomorrow, right, {c}{f:|}?
Whatever you do, don't swim in Lane 4.
Though if you're reeeally confident, I won't stop you.
Well, that's the end of my story.
If the seventh one doesn't show up, the next person will be the last, huh.{p}

On instinct, Hayashi ducked under the lane rope and escaped into the next lane.
It was practically a gamble.
There was no guarantee that whatever was chasing her would just keep swimming straight ahead.
Even so, she had a feeling she'd have a better chance than if she kept swimming where she was.
And that feeling was right.{p}

The thing closing in behind Hayashi kept going straight down Lane 4 at a terrifying speed.
Hayashi got a good look at it.{p}

It was Seto!
Nothing like her graceful form when she was alive: the way she clawed at the water, splashing frantically with a desperate look on her face, made it seem like she was trying to escape from something.
Just like Hayashi a moment ago, right?
And then, as if chasing after Seto, a girl swam past.
Behind that girl came another, and behind that one, another...
A whole line of people swimming down Lane 4, one after another.
Hayashi thought:
Until a moment ago, I was in that line too.
Eventually that strange line disappeared from sight, but they say Hayashi never went near Lane 4 again.{p}

"If I'd kept swimming like that, I'd have died just like Seto.
And I'd have ended up swimming forever as part of that line."
That's what Hayashi told the younger members when she graduated.
I wonder if those people are still swimming even now?
To escape from whatever's coming up behind them...
Never noticing that there's someone in the same situation in front of them, too... you know?
Next time you have swimming class, go check for yourself.
Though you'll be in big trouble if the teacher catches you in Lane 4.
If you're ready for that, why not?
That's the end of my story.
